title: Opt-in tournament stack in the packaged deployment
description: Add the tournament stack to the released deployment as a compose profile that is off by default: Postgres, Redis, the tournament server, and the Caddy routes for /tournaments and /public alongside the app. Turning it on is one documented step (enable the profile, then switch on 'Tournaments' in settings from WI-122). All secrets (database password, the server's signing secret) are generated on the club's server on first start and stored in its own environment file or volume; nothing is defaulted. The tournament server's port is not published to the internet; only Caddy is. Resource limits reflect the footprint measured in WI-142.

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Multi-service deployment design with secret generation and health ordering.

acceptance_criteria: With the profile off, only the app and Caddy run, and the app shows no tournament links
With the profile on, /tournaments (TMX) and /public (public pages) work under the club's own domain over HTTPS
Every secret is generated locally on first start; the compose file contains no password, and startup fails clearly rather than falling back to a default
Only ports 80 and 443 are exposed publicly
Services start in dependency order with health checks, on a server of the documented minimum size
Disabling the profile later leaves tournament data intact on its volume

files_to_create: deploy/init-secrets.sh or an equivalent first-start step in the app CLI
notes: Start from the live production stack captured in WI-113.
The app reaches the server at COURTHIVE_API_URL (default http://courthive-server:8383).

testing_requirements: Bring the stack up from nothing on a clean machine with the profile on and off

context.user_story: As a club operator, I want to switch tournaments on with one step.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
